text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.6% today to $136.27, extending a sharp two-week decline of nearly 10% that accelerated after the company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th. The stock has lost ground as oil prices have weakened—crude is trading around $99.64 per barrel domestically, down from highs earlier in the month—driven by investor uncertainty over Iran tensions following the midterm elections and competing signals about whether conflict or diplomacy will prevail.

The broader pressure reflects a fundamental challenge for oil producers: crude prices remain volatile and middling, not high enough to offset concerns about energy transition and long-term demand. The recent surge in fusion energy development headlines, while not an immediate threat, sits in the background of how investors are thinking about the energy sector's future.
